info.title: Tracepad API
info.summary: Lightweight, self-hosted, OTLP-native store for LLM and agent traces.
info.description: The read API is the product's contract: the UI, the CLI and the MCP server are thin clients over exactly these endpoints, and a feature that is not here does not exist. Responses are flat snake_case JSON with RFC 3339 timestamps and opaque cursors. Every response spends a byte budget on payloads (default 51200, `?budget=` to override): a payload that does not fit is cut at a UTF-8 boundary and replaced by a truncation marker naming where the whole of it lives.

tags.name: raw
tags.description: The archive of export bodies as they arrived, which is what an export replays

tags.name: datasets
tags.description: Datasets of versioned test cases, the runs over them, and the score configs that pin what a score name means

tags.name: admin
tags.description: Projects, keys, retention windows and user-data erasure

get.summary: Liveness and version, no authentication required

post.summary: OTLP/HTTP trace ingest, protobuf or JSON
post.description: The canonical OTLP endpoint. Point any OpenTelemetry SDK at it with `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` and an authorization header. Both OTLP encodings are accepted — `application/x-protobuf` and, per `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL=http/json`, `application/json` with the ids hex-encoded as the OTLP specification prescribes. The response mirrors the request's encoding. A 200 means the spans are committed and fsynced.

schema.description: The same message in the OTLP/JSON encoding, optionally gzipped: `traceId`, `spanId`, `parentSpanId` and the ids inside a link are hex, not base64, and 64-bit integers may be strings or numbers

200.description: Accepted; the body is an ExportTraceServiceResponse carrying partial_success when spans were skipped, in the encoding the request arrived in

415.description: Content-Type is neither application/x-protobuf nor application/json

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

post.summary: OTLP ingest under the Langfuse SDK's path
post.description: The same endpoint as `/v1/traces`, at the path a Langfuse SDK sends to. Setting `LANGFUSE_HOST` to a tracepad is the whole migration.

get.summary: This endpoint map
get.description: Where an agent that has never seen this API starts: every endpoint with a one-line description, plus the link to this document. Needs no key: it says what the API is, never what is in it.

get.summary: The OpenAPI 3.1 document for this API
Version, uptime, database size and ingest counters since start
get.description: Self-diagnosis without a metrics stack. The counters are in-memory and cover this process only, which is what `counters.since` says. Row counts and counters are the asking project's own — `payloads` is absent because it cannot be attributed to one, `projects` is how many tenants share this process (naming none of them), and `size_bytes` is the whole deployment's file on disk.

200.description: What this process knows about itself

size_bytes.description: The database file plus its write-ahead log, for the whole deployment

rows.description: Row counts within the asking project, plus `projects` as a bare tenant count

runs.description: The link between traces and dataset runs, as this project sees it

pinned_traces.description: Traces a live run keeps out of the retention sweep — the size of retention's one exception

orphan_traces.description: Trace deliveries since start that named a run this project does not have; they are stored, and each unknown id is logged once

raw.description: The archive of export bodies: what an export can replay, and what it cannot. Unlike the counters this is on disk, not since start.

enabled.description: Whether accepted bodies are still being kept (TRACEPAD_STORE_RAW)

bytes.description: What the archive occupies on disk, compressed — the number an operator moving `raw_retention_days` is deciding about

traces_before_window.description: Traces whose earliest span started before the oldest batch arrived, and which an export therefore cannot cover. A lower bound: a late export of an old trace lands after the batch line.

counters.description: This project's ingest traffic since the process started

get.summary: List traces newest first, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Rows carry the aggregate columns and never a payload — a listing is for choosing what to fetch. To read one trace whole, follow with `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}`; to go straight to the newest match, use `GET /api/v1/traces/last`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's user id

parameters.name: session_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace's session id

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Exact match on the trace name

parameters.name: tag
parameters.description: Repeatable; a trace must carry every tag given

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `error` keeps traces with at least one failed observation, `ok` keeps the rest

parameters.name: min_cost
parameters.description: Keeps traces whose total cost is at least this much. A trace whose client provided no cost has none and never matches.

parameters.name: fields
parameters.description: Comma-separated subset of the row fields. An unknown name is a 400.

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many rows the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap and the real number is larger

get.summary: The newest trace matching the filters, whole
get.description: The task shortcut: `?status=error&expand=io` answers "why did the last run fail" in one round trip instead of list, filter, get, and one get per observation. Takes every filter of the listing and returns exactly what `GET /api/v1/traces/{id}` returns.

404.description: Nothing matches; the message names the filters that found nothing

get.summary: One trace with its observations as a nested tree
get.description: Children are nested inside their parents, siblings ordered by start time. An observation whose parent has not arrived yet renders at the root with its `parent_observation_id` intact. Payloads ride only with `?expand=io`.

get.summary: The whole input, output and metadata of one observation
get.description: The one endpoint no byte budget applies to: it exists to be the `full` target of every truncation marker, and a budget here would recurse. A span id is unique only inside its trace, so pass `?trace_id=` when the same id appears in more than one — every truncation marker already carries the pair.

parameters.name: trace_id
parameters.description: Optional; required only when the span id is ambiguous within the project

409.description: The span id appears in more than one trace; the message lists the candidates

get.summary: List the raw export bodies oldest first, cursor-paginated
get.description: The archive: every accepted export, kept as it arrived. This is the one listing here whose natural order is forward, because a replay has to preserve arrival order — a receiver that does not upsert by span id must see the spans in the order the world produced them. Follow with `GET /api/v1/raw/{id}` for a body; `tracepad export --otlp` is these two endpoints in a loop.

parameters.name: since
parameters.description: RFC 3339, inclusive, on `received_at`

parameters.name: until
parameters.description: RFC 3339, exclusive, on `received_at`

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

parameters.name: direction
parameters.description: Which way to page from the cursor. This listing runs oldest first, so `next` walks towards newer batches and `prev` back towards older ones; with no cursor, `next` is the oldest page and `prev` the newest. Rows come back oldest first either way

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Adds `total` and `total_capped`: how many batches the filters match, counted up to 100000 — high, because this count answers "how much is this export about to send"

get.summary: One raw export body, in the Content-Type it was received in
get.description: The bytes the client posted, gzip already removed. Exempt from the response budget for the reason `/observations/{id}/io` is: a cut body is not a smaller batch, it is a broken one. `X-Tracepad-Received-At` and `X-Tracepad-Dialect` carry what a client needs to name a file or label a manifest without a second request.

X-Tracepad-Dialect.description: Absent when the mapper claimed nothing

get.summary: List sessions by most recent activity, filtered and cursor-paginated
get.description: Aggregated from the traces that named a session; there is no session table. `from`/`to` bound the *traces*, half-open like the trace listing, so a session appears when any of its traces falls in the window and its totals then describe those traces. To read one session's traces, follow with `GET /api/v1/sessions/{id}`.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Exact match on the user id of a session's traces

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many sessions the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One session: its totals and its traces
get.description: A session is not a stored entity but the set of traces that named it. Every aggregate counts traces: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed, not how many spans did.

total_cost.description: Absent when no trace of the session carried a cost

get.summary: Counts, errors, cost and latency percentiles per bucket
get.description: `unit` says what a bucket counts: grouping by hour, day, environment or release counts traces, and grouping by model counts observations, because a trace has no model. Grouped by release, a trace that named none falls in the bucket with the empty key. An empty range answers with no buckets rather than with fabricated zero rows. Latency percentiles are histogram-based: accurate to a few percent, and stable across the expiry of the raw rows.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Restricts every bucket to one end user. The shape, the groupings and `unit` are unchanged; a `hour` or `day` timeline additionally carries `sessions` per bucket. Statistics for one user trail the raw data by the same rollup lag as the rest

total_cost.description: Absent when nothing in the bucket carried a cost

sessions.description: Present only with `user_id` and an `hour` or `day` grouping: how many of that user's sessions began in this bucket. A session is counted where it starts, so a sum over any range is exact

get.summary: List users by last seen, traffic, cost or errors, cursor-paginated
get.description: Answered from the per-user rollup alone, so it trails the raw data by up to twice the rollup interval: a user first seen minutes ago is not listed yet, and `GET /api/v1/users/{id}` is exact for any id. Every number counts traces, not observations, and `sessions` counts sessions where they started. Sorting is always descending, with ties broken by `user_id`; a user with no costed trace sorts last under `sort=cost`.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Which of the four questions this listing is answering: who was here recently, who runs the most, who costs the most, who fails the most

parameters.name: prefix
parameters.description: Keeps ids starting with this, case-sensitively. A prefix rather than a substring, because an index answers a prefix; the listing is not search

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the last one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the first one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many users the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One user: traffic, sessions, cost, errors and latency
get.description: The rollup plus the live tail — the traces past the rollup's watermark — so the answer is exact for any id, including one the listing has not caught up with. `404` when neither half has seen it. For this user's activity over time, and the breakdown by environment or model, ask `GET /api/v1/stats?user_id=`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user id, as the application set it

post.summary: Write one score or an array of them
post.description: An array is all-or-nothing: one transaction, and one 400 naming the first invalid item. A 201 means the rows are on disk. No Content-Type is required.

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

get.summary: List scores, filtered and cursor-paginated
Fetch one score

delete.summary: Retract one score; no dry run, a re-POST puts it back
delete.description: A score is one row, so there is no echo to type: writing the same id again recreates it.

get.summary: List prompt names with where their labels point
get.description: Alphabetically by name. `direction` reads towards the start of the alphabet, so both ends of the listing cost what one page costs.

get.summary: Fetch one prompt by version, by label, or the latest
get.description: With neither `version` nor `label`, the highest version. `latest` is a virtual label meaning the same thing; there is no implicit `production`.

delete.summary: Delete a prompt with every version and label; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes the name
delete.description: The name's whole history goes at once — versions are never deleted alone. Traces that ran the prompt keep the name and version they recorded: that is a string pair the client sent, not a reference into this table. Without `confirm` it answers with the counts and changes nothing.

200.description: What went, or the dry run of what would

post.summary: Append a version to a prompt
post.description: Versions are append-only and numbered inside the write transaction, so parallel creates produce 1..N with no gaps. A name's type is fixed by its first version. `expect_version` makes the append conditional on the name still being where the author left it.

type.description: Required on the first version of a name

prompt.description: A string for a text prompt, an array of {role, content} messages for a chat one

expect_version.description: The version the author believed this name was at — `0` for a name they believe is new. A mismatch is a `409` naming the version it is actually at, and writes nothing. Absent means append to whatever is there.

409.description: `expect_version` disagrees with the name's current state; nothing was written

version.description: The version the name is actually at; 0 when it does not exist

get.summary: List a prompt's versions, newest first
get.description: Without the bodies: a version list is for picking and diffing. `labels` is every label of the name with the version it points at — the whole map, not the part of it that falls on this page.

labels.description: Every label of the name and the version it points at

get.summary: Unified diff between two versions of a prompt
get.description: A unified text patch over the pretty-printed `prompt` and `config` of the two versions — the format every consumer already reads. Empty when the two versions are identical.

put.summary: Point a label at a version
put.description: The deploy path: promote by moving `production` forward, roll back by moving it back. One row, no new version.

200.description: The version the label pointed at

get.summary: List datasets by name, cursor-paginated

put.summary: Create a dataset or replace its description and metadata
put.description: The envelope only: the items and the version clock are untouched. A dataset also comes into being on the first POST of items to its name.

get.summary: One dataset: its version and counts

delete.summary: Delete a dataset with its items and runs; a dry run until `?confirm=` echoes the name
delete.description: The one destructive act here: every version of every item and every run go with the dataset, and the traces the runs were pinning return to the retention window — they are not deleted. Without `confirm` it answers with the counts and changes nothing.

200.description: What went, or the dry run of what would

post.summary: Add or edit items, one or an array, one version tick for the batch
post.description: All or nothing. The dataset's version advances by exactly one if any item in the batch changed and not at all if none did, so re-posting the same cases is idempotent; `changed` says how many produced a row. An item's id is the idempotency key; an edit is a new row of the same id, and the old one stays readable at every earlier version.

version.description: The dataset's version after the write

changed.description: How many items produced a row; 0 leaves `version` where it was

429.description: The write queue is full; retry after the Retry-After delay

get.summary: The items at a version, whole, in first-appearance order
get.description: Budget-exempt: the consumer is the harness, and a truncated test case is a different test case. Bounded by `limit` and by the body cap at write time. Default `version` is the current one; a version above it is a 400.

version.description: The version the items were resolved at

get.summary: One item as of a version

delete.summary: Archive an item at a new version
delete.description: Nothing is destroyed: the item is gone from the current version and still there at every earlier one. A 404 when the item is unknown or already archived at the current version.

200.description: The version the archive landed on

get.summary: Every row of one item's history, newest first
get.description: Archived rows included, each flagged: an edit is a row and a delete is a row.

post.summary: Open a run over the dataset at its current or a named version
post.description: The run pins the dataset version the harness must fetch its items at, and the response carries it. A client-supplied `id` makes the call retry-safe: a known id answers 200 with the existing run unchanged. The store never executes anything — the harness stamps `tracepad.run_id` and `tracepad.item_id` on the spans it exports, and closes the run with `/finish`.

metadata.description: What was being tried, in the harness's own terms

dataset_version.description: The version to pin; the current one when absent, and a 400 above it

200.description: The run that already had this id

get.summary: List a dataset's runs newest first, cursor-paginated
List the project's runs newest first, filtered by dataset and status, cursor-paginated
get.description: Every dataset's runs in one listing, ordered by `(created_at, id)` like the per-dataset one and paged by the same cursor shape. The rows are the run objects without `summary`: a page of runs is for choosing one. `?count=` adds the capped total the filters match.

parameters.name: dataset
parameters.description: Exact dataset name; a name outside the grammar is a 400

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Keeps the runs in one state

next_cursor.description: Pass back as `?cursor=` for the next page; null on the oldest one

prev_cursor.description: Pass back with `?direction=prev` for the page before; null on the newest one

total.description: Present only with `?count=`: how many runs the filters match, capped at 1000

total_capped.description: Present only with `?count=`: the count stopped at the cap

get.summary: One run with its summary
get.description: The run object with `summary`: how much of the dataset it covered, what its traffic cost, what its scores came to, and which models and prompts it actually ran. The listing leaves the summary out.

delete.summary: Delete a run, releasing its traces to the retention window
delete.description: One row of bookkeeping. The traces it held are not deleted; they stop being pinned and live as long as retention says.

released_traces.description: How many traces the run was keeping out of the sweep

get.summary: The run's items with the attempts it made at each
get.description: The items of the run's dataset version in first-appearance order, each with the traces of the run that answered it. `output` is the trace's root observation's output; `expected_output` and `output` are budgeted and cut with a marker naming where the whole payload lives. `?unknown=true` appends the run's traces that no item of its version accounts for.

parameters.name: unknown
parameters.description: `true` appends the traces whose item is not in the run's dataset version, after the known items

get.summary: Two runs of one dataset side by side
get.description: Per score name: each run's aggregate, the delta between the means, and how many items improved, regressed or stayed — `improved` and `regressed` only for names whose config gives a direction, `changed` for the rest. Then the items, paginated, each with its per-name pair and verdict. Equality is exact. Runs of different datasets, and a run against itself, are a 400.

post.summary: Close a run as finished, or as failed with a reason
post.description: The store never infers completion: a run stays `running` until the harness says otherwise. A run closed twice is a 409. Linking does not stop at finish — a late span of a trace that started inside the run still belongs to it.

get.summary: List score configs by name
get.description: Whole, not paged: a project declares a handful of names.

put.summary: Create or replace the config that binds a score name
put.description: Declarative: the whole config, every time, and a re-PUT of the same body is a no-op. From then on a score posted under this name must have the config's `data_type`, a numeric value inside `min`/`max`, a categorical value among `categories`; a violating score fails its batch with a 400 naming it. Scores already stored are never re-validated.

get.summary: One score config

delete.summary: Remove a score config; the scores it admitted stay

get.summary: List projects
get.description: The admin token sees every project; a project key sees its own and nothing else.

parameters.name: include
parameters.description: `deleted` adds soft-deleted projects with their purge dates. Admin token only.

200.description: The projects the caller may see

post.summary: Create a project and its first key pair
post.description: The secret key is in this response and in no other: only its hash is stored. A name inside another project's grace window is a 409 naming the restorable one.

201.description: The project and its one-time secret

get.summary: One project with its retention windows
get.description: A soft-deleted project's own key still reaches this one, so that a caller about to restore can see what it is restoring and until when.

patch.summary: Rename a project or move its retention windows
patch.description: Renaming needs the admin token; the windows are the project's own business. `null` means keep forever. A window that shrinks is destructive: without `confirm` it answers with the preview, and it applies only when `confirm` echoes the project's name.

retention_days.description: How long a trace is kept after it arrived; null keeps it forever. Bounded because a window becomes a nanosecond cutoff, and a large enough one would overflow into the future and match every row — "forever" is null, not a big number.

raw_retention_days.description: The window for stored OTLP bodies; null follows retention_days

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the hourly statistics rollup, measured by the hour a row summarizes; null keeps it forever, which is the default. The rollup outlives the traces it summarizes, so shortening this window destroys history the trace sweep spares — it asks for the same confirmation the other two do.

200.description: The project as it is now, or the dry run of a window that shrinks

delete.summary: Soft-delete a project, restorable for seven days
delete.description: The keys stop authenticating immediately and the project vanishes from listings; the data is destroyed by the sweeper after a fixed seven-day grace. Admin token only, even for one's own project. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview.

200.description: The dry run: what deleting it would eventually destroy

202.description: Deleted, with the date the data is purged

post.summary: Undo a soft delete inside its grace window
post.description: No confirmation: it destroys nothing. Reachable with the project's own key even while deleted, so that a deployment without an admin token can still undo one.

get.summary: List a project's public keys
get.description: The secrets are not here because they are not anywhere: only their hashes are stored.

post.summary: Mint a key pair; the secret is shown once
post.description: Several active pairs are what makes rotation zero-downtime: create the new one, move the SDKs, revoke the old.

201.description: The new pair, secret included this once

delete.description: Revoking a project's last key stops its ingest, so that one is a dry run until `confirm` echoes the project's name.

200.description: The key is gone, or the dry run for the last one

delete.summary: Erase everything stored about one user
delete.description: Erases the queryable stores synchronously: the traces filed under the user id, their observations, payloads and scores. Raw OTLP bodies are not touched — they are an archive expiring on the raw retention window, which docs/retention.md documents together with what that means for an erasure request. Without `confirm` it answers with the preview; the echo here is the user id.

200.description: What was erased, or the dry run of what would be

basicKeys.description: `base64(public key:secret key)`, the shape a Langfuse SDK sends

adminToken.description: `TRACEPAD_ADMIN_TOKEN`, sent in the same header as a project key. Required for everything cross-project and for deleting a project. A server with none configured answers 403 and says so.

From.name: from
From.description: RFC 3339, inclusive. The range is half-open, so walking a timeline never reports a row twice.

Environment.name: environment
Environment.description: Exact match on the environment a trace ran in

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Out of range is a 400, not a silent clamp

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: The opaque `next_cursor` or `prev_cursor` of a previous page

Direction.name: direction
Direction.description: Which way to page from the cursor. With no cursor, `next` is the newest page and `prev` the oldest — both ends are a direction rather than an offset. Rows come back newest first either way

Count.name: count
Count.description: Adds `total` and `total_capped`: how many rows the filters match, counted up to 1000. Off by default, because the count changes with the filters and not with the page

Search.name: q
Search.description: Full-text search over one field of one observation — input, output, metadata, name or status message — or over the trace name. Words (all must occur), `"quoted phrases"`, `prefix*`. Words, not substrings: `error` does not find `errors`, `err*` finds both. Case and diacritics are folded, identifiers split on punctuation, and only the first 64 KiB of each payload is indexed. A `q` with no word in it is a 400

Release.name: release
Release.description: Exact match on the deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`

Version.name: version
Version.description: Exact match on the version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version`

ObservationType.name: type
ObservationType.description: Keeps traces with at least one observation of this kind. Exact: `generation` does not match `embedding`. A value outside the list is a 400

Prompt.name: prompt
Prompt.description: `name` or `name@version`: keeps traces with at least one observation that ran this prompt, at any version or at that one. A version is a run of digits after the last `@` with a name in front of it; every other string is a name, `@` included — `@acme/support`, `team@acme/answer`, `name@latest` and `svc@-1` all filter as names. A label is not a version

RunFilter.name: run_id
RunFilter.description: Keeps the traces of one dataset run. A value of another shape is a 400: the ingest mapper claims nothing else into the column, so it could only match nothing

ItemFilter.name: item_id
ItemFilter.description: Keeps the attempts at one dataset item, across runs unless `run_id` narrows it

Expand.name: expand
Expand.description: `io` inlines each observation's input, output and metadata, each cut to an equal share of the remaining budget with a truncation marker naming the rest

Budget.name: budget
Budget.description: Byte budget for the payloads of this response; the structure is never truncated

Confirm.name: confirm
Confirm.description: The name of the project — or the id of the user — being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with a preview; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

ConfirmName.name: confirm
ConfirmName.description: The name of the dataset being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the counts; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

ConfirmPromptName.name: confirm
ConfirmPromptName.description: The name of the prompt being destroyed. Without it the endpoint changes nothing and answers with the counts; a value that does not match is a 400 that also changes nothing.

DatasetName.name: name
DatasetName.description: The prompt-name grammar: one URL path segment

DatasetVersion.name: version
DatasetVersion.description: The dataset version to resolve the items at; the current one when absent. Above the current version it is a 400. A run's `dataset_version` is what to pass here

ScoreConfigName.name: name
ScoreConfigName.description: A score name: any name a score may carry can have a config

BadRequest.description: The request cannot mean what it says: an unknown query parameter, a malformed value, a limit out of range

Unauthorized.description: The credentials do not resolve to a project

NotFound.description: No such thing in this project

Forbidden.description: The credentials are good but do not reach this far: cross-project administration needs the admin token

Conflict.description: The stored state already answers differently: a name that is taken, a project that is already deleted

Error.description: The one error shape the whole surface uses

TraceRow.description: A trace as it appears in a listing: aggregates only, never a payload. A field the trace never carried is absent rather than empty.

release.description: The deployment the trace ran in, from `langfuse.release` or the resource's `service.version`

version.description: The version of the trace's own logic, from `langfuse.version`

run_id.description: The dataset run this trace belongs to, from `tracepad.run_id`; absent on ordinary traffic. No foreign key stands behind it: a trace may name a run the project does not have

item_id.description: The dataset item this trace answered, from `tracepad.item_id`; never present without `run_id`

timestamp.description: When the earliest observation of the trace started

total_cost.description: Summed over the observations whose client provided cost; absent when none did

ttft_ms.description: The wait before the first token: the earliest completion start among the trace's observations, minus the trace's own start. Absent when no observation carried one, and negative when a client's completion start precedes its span

Match.description: Where the search hit, present only with `?q=`: the observation and field with the best score among the trace's hits, and a window of the text around the first term. Hits are not marked up — a client that highlights folds the query terms the way the tokenizer does.

observation_id.description: The observation that matched; null when the trace's own name did

snippet.description: At most 160 characters, cut on word boundaries

SessionRow.description: The roll-up over the traces of one session. Every number counts traces, not observations: `error_count` is how many of the session's traces failed.

id.description: The session id, as the application set it

total_cost.description: Summed over the traces that carried a cost; absent when none did

UserRow.description: The roll-up over one end user's traffic. Every number counts traces, not observations: `error_count` is how many of the user's traces failed. `first_seen` and `last_seen` are rounded down to the hour the rollup keeps, except on `GET /api/v1/users/{id}`, where the live tail makes them exact to the second.

user_id.description: The user id, as the application set it

total_cost.description: Summed over the traces that carried a cost; absent when none did

sessions.description: How many sessions of this user have begun. A session with no user id on its traces belongs to no user and is not counted here

first_seen.description: The start of the earliest hour the rollup still holds for this user; it moves forward as `stats_retention_days` sweeps

RawBatch.description: One archived export body, described. The bytes themselves are at `GET /api/v1/raw/{id}`.

id.description: The batch's id; the path segment of the body endpoint

received_at.description: When the server accepted it, which is the order a replay preserves

dialect.description: Which attribute vocabulary the mapper recognised in it; empty when it claimed nothing

content_type.description: The media type the body is in, which is what a replay posts it under. Batches stored before schema 0012 read as `application/x-protobuf`.

content_encoding.description: How the client compressed it on the wire, for provenance. The stored body is decoded, so a replay does not have to unwrap two layers.

size_bytes.description: The decoded length — what a fetch of the body returns — and not the compressed length the row occupies

Observation.description: One span. `children` holds the spans that named it as their parent and is absent for a leaf.

parent_observation_id.description: The observation this one ran under, whenever it named one. Nested children carry it too; an observation whose parent is not in this trace renders at the root and still carries it.

type.description: What kind of step this was. A span whose client named no type is classified: a model attribute makes it a generation, a zero-duration childless span an event, anything else a span

completion_start_time.description: When the first token came back, as the client reported it — stored uncorrected, so it may precede `start_time`

ttft_ms.description: `completion_start_time` minus `start_time`; absent when either is missing

input_bytes.description: The uncompressed size of `input`, present whether or not the payload itself is inlined

PromptLink.description: The prompt the client said this observation ran. Recorded as sent and resolved against no registry — the store may not manage this prompt at all, and a label that points at nothing is still a label. Absent when the client named none.

version.description: Null when the client named a prompt without a whole-number version

Expansion.description: Present only when `?expand=io` was refused: a trace with more payloads than the budget can carry markers for gets none of them and this instead. Nothing is unreachable — the tree lists every observation id — and `budget_needed` is what to retry `?budget=` with.

payloads.description: How many payloads the trace holds.

budget_needed.description: The budget that would carry a marker for each of them. Never clamped to the maximum, so it may exceed what `?budget=` accepts.

retryable.description: Whether `budget_needed` is a budget this server would accept. False means no budget can carry this many markers — read the payloads one at a time instead.

Truncation.description: A payload too large for this response's budget. `full` is the URL that returns it whole; `trace_id` and `observation_id` are the same target for a consumer that speaks tools rather than URLs.

size.description: The payload's full size in bytes

preview.description: A prefix of the payload, cut on a UTF-8 boundary

ScoreInput.description: One judgement. A score needs a trace or a session, and either a `value` or a `string_value`.

id.description: Generated when absent; writing the same id again replaces the score

data_type.description: Inferred when absent: a `value` makes it numeric, a `string_value` makes it text

timestamp.description: Event time; defaults to receive time

prompt.description: Stored and returned verbatim; interpolation is the client's job

Project.description: A project with its retention windows. `deleted_at` and `purge_at` are present only while a soft delete is inside its grace window.

retention_days.description: null means the data is kept forever, which is the default

stats_retention_days.description: The window for the statistics rollup, which outlives the traces it summarizes; null means it is kept forever, which is the default

purge_at.description: When the sweeper destroys the data; seven days after the delete, and not configurable

NewKey.description: A freshly minted key pair. The secret appears here and nowhere else, ever.

DryRun.description: What a destructive request would do, which is what it does until it is confirmed

oldest.description: Arrival of the oldest affected row; absent when nothing is affected

affected_runs.description: User-data erasure only: the dataset runs that would lose traces to it, because erasure overrides the pin a run puts on them

traces.description: How many of the run's traces this erasure would take

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

Deletion.description: What a confirmed destructive request actually removed

Dataset.description: A named, versioned set of test cases. `version` advances by one on every write that changes the item set; `item_count` is the live items at that version.

DatasetItemInput.description: One test case. The three bodies are opaque JSON the store never reads inside; the source pair is a note about where the case came from, not a reference.

id.description: Generated when absent; the same id again is an edit of the same item

DatasetItem.description: One item as of a version. `version` is the dataset version the row was written at, which may be earlier than the version it was read at; `seq` is the item's place in the listing, fixed at its first appearance. `archived` appears on the history listing only.

Run.description: A run of a dataset: the container the harness opened, the version it pinned, and how it ended. `finished_at` is null while it is running.

RunSummary.description: How the run went, computed at read time: a run keeps taking late spans, and a stored summary would be wrong in exactly the window somebody is watching.

items.description: Coverage of the dataset at the run's version. `unknown` counts the run's traces that no item of that version accounts for — a harness that ran newer cases, a mistyped id, or a trace that named a run and no item.

traces.description: The run's traffic. `error_count` counts traces that failed, not observations; percentiles are exact over the run's traces, not the bucketed ones of `/stats`.

attempts_max.description: The largest number of traces one item got

total_cost.description: Null when no attempt carried a cost

scores.description: One entry per score name the run carried. `mean`/`min`/`max` for numeric and boolean names, `distribution` for categorical ones, and `count` alone for text.

models.description: Derived from the run's observations, not from what the harness declared

data_type.description: The type the run's scores under this name actually used — the commonest one when they used more than a single type. A config declares what is accepted next and never re-types what is stored, so this can differ from `GET /score-configs/{name}`.

direction.description: From the name's config, and only for a numeric or boolean `data_type`, the two that have an axis; null otherwise, which is what makes a comparison say `changed` rather than `improved`

RunItems.description: The run's items with their attempts, in first-appearance order.

RunItem.description: One case and the attempts the run made at it. An unknown row — a trace whose item is not in the run's version — carries `unknown: true`, no `seq` and no case body; a trace that named no item at all has a null `id`.

RunAttempt.description: One trace of the run: what it cost, how it went, what its root observation answered and how it was scored.

output.description: The trace's root observation's output — the earliest starting observation with no parent — or null when it carried none

RunComparison.description: Two runs of one dataset side by side. `same_version` is false when the dataset moved between them, and the items outside the intersection are labelled rather than dropped.

metadata.description: Only the metadata keys the two runs disagree about, both values

traces.description: Both runs' traffic, and the cost delta

delta.description: b minus a; null when either side carried no cost

ComparedSide.description: One run's aggregate for a score name: the mean for a numeric or boolean name, the distribution for a categorical one, the count alone for text.

ComparedScore.description: One score name across both runs. A name with a direction reports `improved`/`regressed`/`same`; one without reports `changed`/`same`, because without a direction there is no better.

a.description: Null when that run never carried the name

delta.description: b's mean minus a's; null unless both are numbers

ComparedItem.description: One case in both runs. `in` says which side had it: `both`, `a` or `b` when the item is in both versions, and `only_in_version_a` / `only_in_version_b` when the dataset moved between the runs.

scores.description: Per score name both runs scored: the two values, the delta for numbers, and the verdict

DatasetDeletion.description: What deleting a dataset takes: its live items, its runs, and the traces those runs were pinning — which are released, not deleted. `confirm` is present on the dry run only.

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

PromptDeletion.description: What deleting a prompt name takes: every version of it and every label pointing into it. `confirm` and `note` are present on the dry run only; `deleted` on the confirmed answer only.

confirm.description: Send this back as `?confirm=` to make it happen

ScoreConfigInput.description: What a score name means. `direction` is required for numeric and boolean names and forbidden for categorical and text ones; `min`/`max` are numeric only, with `min` at most `max`; `categories` is required for categorical names and forbidden otherwise.

direction.description: Which way is better; `none` for a number that is typed and bounded but not judged
